title: Noisy last-coordinate splitting identity
statement: Let $n,m\ge0$, let $P:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ and $\rho\in\mathbb R$, and let $f$ and $g_1,\ldots,g_m$ be real-valued functions on $\{0,1\}^{n+1}$. Write $f_0,f_1$ and $g_{j,0},g_{j,1}$ for their restrictions to the last coordinate, and put $a_f=(f_0+f_1)/2$, $d_f=(f_0-f_1)/2$, with $a_{g_j}=(g_{j,0}+g_{j,1})/2$ and $d_{g_j}=(g_{j,0}-g_{j,1})/2$. Then the uniform-cube expectation of $L(1,B(x)^2)$, where $B=T_\rho d_f(x)$, the first argument of $L$ is $A=T_\rho a_f(x)$, and its vector arguments are $U=V(T_\rho a_f,(T_\rho a_{g_j})_j)(x)$ and $W=V(T_\rho d_f,(T_\rho d_{g_j})_j)(x)$, equals the average of $F_P$ on the two last-coordinate restrictions: $\bigl(F_P(T_\rho f_0,(T_\rho d_f,T_\rho g_{0})) + F_P(T_\rho f_1,(T_\rho d_f,T_\rho g_{1}))\bigr)/2$. Here $T_\rho$ is the Fourier noise operator, $V$ consists of the coordinate half-differences followed by the listed additional coordinates, and $F_P$ is the uniform expectation of the square root of $P$ of the function squared plus the squared Euclidean length of $V$.
hypotheses_covered: $g$ is an $m$-tuple of real-valued functions on $\{0,1\}^{n+1}$
replaced: For a profile $P:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, a real function $h$ on a uniform Boolean cube, and a vector $k$ of real functions on that cube, put $V(h,k)(x)=((D_i h(x))_i,(k_j(x))_j)$ and $F_P(h,k)=\mathbb E\sqrt{P(h)^2+\|V(h,k)\|_2^2}$, where $D_i$ is the coordinate half-difference. Let $f$ be a real function and $g$ a vector of $m$ real functions on $\{0,1\}^{n+1}$. Put $f_b(x)=f(x,b)$, $g_b(x)=g(x,b)$, $a_f=(f_0+f_1)/2$, $d_f=(f_0-f_1)/2$, and define $a_g,d_g$ componentwise. Let $T_\rho$ denote Boolean noise with real correlation $\rho$, whose Fourier multiplier on a set of size $k$ is $\rho^k$. For each $x$, put $a=T_\rho a_f(x)$, $b=T_\rho d_f(x)$, $u=V(T_\rho a_f,T_\rho a_g)(x)$, and $v=V(T_\rho d_f,T_\rho d_g)(x)$. Then $\mathbb E_x\frac12\sum_{\epsilon\in\{-1,1\}}\sqrt{P(a+\epsilon b)^2+b^2+\|u+\epsilon v\|_2^2}=\bigl(F_P(T_\rho f_0,(T_\rho d_f,T_\rho g_0))+F_P(T_\rho f_1,(T_\rho d_f,T_\rho g_1))\bigr)/2$.
